title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page is part of the proof of 'Théorème 2' on the previous page. That theorem says the functor K -> (Pi_K -> Pi_Q), from finitely generated fields of characteristic 0 (over Q) to profinite groupoids, or outer profinite groups, over Pi_Q = Gal(Qbar/Q), is faithful. If two embeddings f, g : K -> K' induce the same outer homomorphism Pi_{K'} -> Pi_K over Pi_Q, then f = g.

Step 1. Write K = colim A_i, with A_i finitely generated (regular) Q-subalgebras, so eta = Spec K = lim U_i, U_i = Spec A_i. Work with the geometric parts. Choosing a geometric point eta-bar (an algebraic closure K-bar), the geometric fundamental group of K is pi_K = Gal(K-bar / K.Qbar) = lim_i pi_1(U_i-bar, eta-bar), where U_i-bar = U_i (x)_Q Qbar. The underlined 'k' and 'Qbar' under the formula indicate that k means Q here.

Step 2. It suffices to prove f|A_i = g|A_i for every i. This uses that the hypothesis gives pi_1(f_i^*) = pi_1(g_i^*) : pi_{K'} -> pi_1(U_i-bar) as outer homomorphisms.

Step 3. Fix i. Write K' = colim A'_j, with A'_j containing f(A_i) and g(A_i). Then pi_{K'} = lim_j pi_1(V_j-bar, eta'-bar), with V_j-bar = Spec(A'_j) (x)_Q Qbar. Choose the V_j regular (normal suffices).
- The transition maps are then induced by dense open immersions of normal connected schemes, hence surjective on pi_1.
- So pi_{K'} -> pi_1(V_j-bar) is surjective.
- Hence equality of f^*, g^* : pi_{K'} -> pi_1(U_i-bar) as outer homomorphisms implies equality of the induced outer homomorphisms pi_1(V_j-bar) -> pi_1(U_i-bar). If f^* = inn(gamma) o g^* on pi_{K'}, the same gamma works after passing to the surjective quotient.

Step 4. So f_i = g_i (i.e. f = g) will follow from a more general 'geometric finiteness' statement. This is Corollary 1 on the next page: two morphisms f, g : X -> Y of reduced finite-type schemes over an algebraically closed field that agree on pi_1 as outer homomorphisms are equal, under conditions on Y:
- (a) If Y embeds in a semi-abelian group, f and g agree up to translation; for this it is enough that H_1(-, Z_ell) agrees.
- (b) If Y is an 'elementary' variety (successive fibrations in curves, presumably hyperbolic) and f is dominant, then f = g.

Purpose: the faithfulness half of the anabelian 'section/hom conjecture' for finitely generated fields. The proof reduces the arithmetic statement over Pi_Q to purely geometric rigidity of morphisms detected by pi_1.
errors: The page only uses the geometric (pi_1 of the base change to Qbar) part of the hypothesis. This is fine because f (x) Qbar = g (x) Qbar implies f = g, but it is left implicit.

Implicit requirements are not stated here. To apply Corollary 1(b), the U_i must be chosen as elementary fibrations (Artin good neighbourhoods); this is possible locally in characteristic 0. The maps V_j -> U_i must also be dominant; they are, since f and g come from field embeddings and so hit the generic point.
The transcribed formula 'V_j-bar = Spec(A_j) (x) Qbar' should read A'_j.

ideas.what: Writing the geometric absolute Galois group of a finitely generated field as the projective limit of geometric etale pi_1 of its regular affine models, with surjective transition maps.
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental group of the generic point as a limit of pi_1 of dense opens (SGA1 V.8 / IX.5 surjectivity for normal schemes)

ideas.what: Reduction of faithfulness of K -> Pi_K over Pi_Q to the statement that morphisms between suitable varieties are determined by their outer action on geometric pi_1.
ideas.modern_name: Faithfulness part of the anabelian conjecture for finitely generated fields (Hom-form)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (conjecture, letter to Faltings 1983 / Esquisse); full result by Pop (1990s) and Mochizuki
ideas.where_published: Possibly in the Malgoire-edited 'La Longue Marche' material; the conjecture itself appears in the Faltings letter and the Esquisse.

ideas.what: 'Geometric finiteness': rigidity of maps into semi-abelian varieties (up to translation, detected by H_1 Z_ell) and into elementary fibrations of curves (detected by pi_1).
ideas.modern_name: Albanese rigidity; pi_1-rigidity of dominant maps to hyperbolic K(pi,1) varieties
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Albanese/Lang); anabelian context Grothendieck, Nakamura, Tamagawa

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean, standard reduction step in the proof of faithfulness for the anabelian functor on finitely generated fields. The ideas are well known and likely appear in the Longue Marche material. Nothing beyond expected unpublished detail.
transcription_corrections: The underlined 'k' and 'Qbar' below the formula for U_i-bar are an annotation meaning k = Q.
'Donc l'égalité f = g (càd f = g)' is likely 'Donc l'égalité f_i = g_i (càd f = g)'.
'pi_1(V_j)', 'pi_1(U_i)' at the end are written with bars: pi_1(V_j-bar) -> pi_1(U_i-bar).
